headline: Acceleration is the rate of change in speed—it's not about going fast, but about speeding up
universal_truth: What matters isn't just where you are or how fast you're going, but whether you're accelerating or decelerating
fun_facts: A falling object accelerates at 9.8 m/s² due to gravity—it gains about 22 mph every second
The human body can survive about 5g of acceleration; fighter pilots can handle 9g with training
A Tesla Model S can accelerate 0-60 mph in under 2 seconds—faster than most sports cars
discussion_questions: Is your progress accelerating or decelerating?
What would cause your growth to accelerate?
When have you felt momentum building?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A car going 60 mph isn't accelerating if it stays at 60. A car going 10 mph but speeding up to 20 is accelerating. Acceleration isn't speed—it's change in speed. It's about whether you're gaining or losing momentum.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Speed tells you how fast you're going now. But are you speeding up or slowing down? That's often more important.
cliff.prompt: Why is acceleration more important than speed?

options.text: Acceleration determines future speed—positive acceleration means you'll go faster; negative means you'll slow down; it predicts trajectory
options.response: Yes. Speed is a snapshot; acceleration is a trend. Going slow but accelerating means you'll be going fast soon. Going fast but decelerating means you won't stay fast.

options.text: Current speed matters more—it's what's actually happening
options.response: Current speed matters, but trajectory often matters more for planning...

q1.title: Rate of Change
q1.script: Acceleration is change in speed over time. It's the rate of change. This meta-level thinking—not just what, but how it's changing—is powerful in physics and in life.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Rate of Change"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Positive and Negative
q2.script: Positive acceleration speeds you up. Negative acceleration (deceleration) slows you down. Both require force. Coasting means no acceleration—speed stays constant until something changes.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Growth Acceleration
q3.script: In learning, career, skills—are you accelerating? Early in a skill, acceleration is high. Later, it often slows. Deliberate practice, new challenges, better methods can reignite acceleration.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What matters isn't just where you are or how fast you're going, but whether you're accelerating or decelerating. Watch your trajectory.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 224. Tomorrow, we'll explore what slows things down—resistance. Until then, check if your growth is accelerating or plateauing.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Acceleration Check - Gaining or Losing Momentum?
growTrack.activity: Pick a skill or goal. Is your rate of progress increasing (acceleration), steady (coasting), or decreasing (deceleration)? If decelerating, what could reignite acceleration? New challenges, different methods, renewed motivation?
